claim: Of the three candidates, only pdfquill both supports digital signatures and has an allowed licence (MIT); paperforge supports signatures but is AGPL-3.0, and inkleaf is Apache-2.0 but can't sign.
ask: Choose between pdfquill, accepting that it has had no release in 14 months, or paperforge, which needs legal to approve the AGPL licence first.
stakes: Choosing pdfquill risks having to fork and patch it ourselves if a bug or security issue appears; choosing paperforge means waiting on legal, and if legal rejects AGPL we can't use it at all.
